slides.heading: Auxiliary (Helping) Verbs
bullets: Auxiliary verbs help conjugate other verbs:  be, have, do, shall, will, can, may, must.
They build tenses and forms:  “I have gone,” “she will sing,” “you must go.”
The helping verb comes first; the main verb follows.
Some (do, be, have) can also stand alone as main verbs:  “He does well.”

slides.heading: Practice — Find the Helping Verb
slides.instruction: Name the helping (auxiliary) verb in each sentence.

slides.heading: Principal Parts
bullets: Every verb has three Principal Parts: the present, the past, and the perfect participle.
love — loved — loved.   ·   go — went — gone.   ·   see — saw — seen.
From these three forms, all the tenses can be built.
Conjugation is simply giving a verb in order through its modes, tenses, persons, and numbers.

slides.heading: Regular & Irregular Verbs
bullets: A Regular Verb forms its past and participle by adding -d or -ed:  love, loved, loved.
An Irregular Verb changes the word instead:  go, went, gone;  see, saw, seen.
Most English verbs are regular; a few dozen common ones are irregular.
The irregular ones must simply be learned by practice.

slides.heading: Practice — Regular or Irregular?
slides.instruction: Tell whether each verb is regular or irregular.

slides.heading: Practice — Give the Principal Parts
slides.instruction: Give the past and the perfect participle of each verb.

slides.heading: The Coordinate Forms
bullets: Besides the plain form, a verb has three coordinate forms.
Progressive — action going on (be + -ing):  “I am writing.”
Emphatic — for emphasis (do):  “I do write.”  “He did go.”
Interrogative — for asking:  “Do you write?”  “Did he go?”

slides.heading: Practice — Which Form?
slides.instruction: Tell whether each verb is progressive, emphatic, or interrogative.

slides.heading: Common Verb Errors
bullets: Irregular verbs never add -ed:  “threw,” not “throwed”; “brought,” not “bringed.”
Use the past participle with a helper:  “I have seen,” not “I have saw.”
Use the plain past by itself:  “I saw,” not “I seen.”
Watch the tricky pairs:  drank/drunk, rang/rung, went/gone, wore/worn.

slides.heading: Practice — Fix the Verb
slides.instruction: Each sentence has a verb mistake. Give the correct word.

items: What are the principal parts of a verb?
answers: A helping verb used to conjugate others.
Be, have, do, shall, will, can, may, must.
The present, the past, and the perfect participle.
One that forms its past and participle by adding -ed.
One that changes its form instead of adding -ed.
